A Caelza bug report from this phone is attached: versions, states and the end of each log, with secrets blanked.
Install the Runtime (one download from the project\'s releases), then start it. The dashboard appears here once the gateway answers.
That did not work: %1$s. Nothing was changed; you can try again or skip this for now.

I\'m the guide inside Caelza. In a few steps I\'ll get this phone to its first working turn, and I\'ll say what each step does and why. Nothing here is a trick question. Every step can be skipped and done later from the dashboard.

The Runtime is the program that runs your agent. It comes from this project\'s releases: one download, checked against its checksum and tried out before it is kept. I keep the last version that worked, so a later one that misbehaves can\'t strand you.
The Runtime is installed (version %1$s). Good! On to the brain.
The Runtime has to be installed first; it is the program that stores these settings. Back to that step.

Two doors. Free and local: a small DeepSeek model runs on this phone, offline, and nobody else sees your words. Or bring your own key: a provider such as Anthropic or OpenAI runs a bigger model for the agent. Either way I run too, as the guide. You can change this any time on the dashboard.
The download is the model plus llama.cpp, the small program that runs it. Wi-Fi is a good idea. The files are checked against their published checksums before anything uses them.
That worked! %1$s is on this phone and the Runtime knows where to find it.

An API key is a password for a model provider. Caelza keeps it encrypted on this device and only ever sends it to that provider. Pick the provider, keep or change the model name, and paste the key. You can swap it later with one command.
That key looks too short. Paste the whole thing from the provider\'s page; it is one long word.
That worked! The agent runs on %1$s, and so do I.

Shizuku gives Caelza shell-level control of this phone without root: that is how the agent uninstalls bloatware or reads the screen. It has to be started again after every reboot unless the phone is rooted. If you don\'t have it, you can add it later; the sensors work without it, so nothing is lost.
Shizuku is not installed. It is a free app at shizuku.rikka.app; this step waits for you.

Each one is for one thing. Camera: a photo when you ask for one. Microphone: a recording when you ask. Location: where the phone is. Notification access: what is waiting in the status bar. A permission you don\'t grant just means that tool says so instead of working; nothing breaks.

Android puts apps to sleep to save battery. Caelza runs a small service that has to stay awake to answer you, so I\'d like it exempted. It costs a little battery. You can take it back any time in Settings.
Exempt from battery optimisation: Caelza stays awake.
Not exempt yet: Android may put Caelza to sleep.
This phone has no screen for that setting; look for Battery › App battery usage in Settings.
A hub, if you want one

Optional. If you have a laptop or a server, Tailscale (a private network between your own devices) lets a Runtime there reach this phone\'s Body, and a bigger model there can do the thinking. Nothing to do now; the Fleet page of the docs has the one-liner when you want it.
Let\'s start the Runtime. The dashboard appears as soon as it answers, and you\'ll find me in the agent picker if anything on it needs explaining.
